column1: # layout in partitions.csv is the better arrangement and it is what this
# project recommends — but ESP32-WROVER-E-N16R8 is easy to buy as a bare
# surface-mount module and hard to buy as a board with pins on it. The
# assembled dev boards you can order in an evening are mostly 8 MB.
# Given the choice between "the recommended build needs a part you have to
# solder a carrier for" and "give up one OTA slot and four megabytes of
# animations"
column2: the second is obviously right for most people.

column1: # WHAT YOU LOSE
#   * One app slot. The 16 MB table has factory + ota_0 + ota_1
#     can roll back to the *previous* update. Here there is factory + ota_0:
#     an update rolls back to the factory image
#     never written. You keep the property that matters — a car with a working
#     stereo — and lose the ability to step back one version rather than to
#     the beginning.
#   * 4.5 MB of movie space. 0x330000 is about 3.2 MB
#     800 KB for a 256x64 scene is four of them
#     bundled set packs to 1.9 MB today
column2: so this is not tight yet.

column1: #   * 1.7 MB of SPIFFS. Photos
# The app slots are NOT reduced. 1.875 MB is measured against a 1.67 MB image
# and shrinking it to claw back movie space would be trading a hard failure
# (an update that does not fit) for a soft one (fewer animations).
# Build with:  idf.py -DDECK_FLASH=8 build
# or:          python3 tools/deckctl.py build --flash 8
# Offsets are exact: the table ends on 0x800000 with no gap and no overlap.
